```text
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::movePiece
Summary: Executes a legal move on the 2D board array: transfers the piece at the source square to the
         destination square, increments the game move counter, and refreshes the console output.
         The move is assumed to have already passed validation by the caller.
Algorithm:
  1. If move is null, source or destination is null, or game.getPiece(source) is null, return without effect.
  2. Let piece = game.getPiece(source).
  3. Set game.getBoard()[destination.x][destination.y] = piece.
  4. Set game.getBoard()[source.x][source.y] = null.
  5. Increment game.numMoves by 1.
  6. Call game.refreshOutput() to update the console.
Related Features: board, numMoves, configuration, currentPlayer (inherited from Game)
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input: move (Move) - the move to execute; source must contain a piece, destination is the new position.
Output: void - no return value.
Pre-condition: move is non-null; source contains a piece; the move has already been validated as legal;
               source and destination are within board bounds.
Post-condition: The source square is null; the destination square contains the moved piece; game.numMoves
               has been incremented by 1; the console has been refreshed.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Aggregates the legal moves of every piece belonging to the given player by delegating to each
         piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position) and concatenating the results without further filtering.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize an empty result list `allMoves`.
  2. Determine the player's piece positions by scanning the board for pieces whose `player` equals
     the supplied player.
  3. For each such piece at place `p`:
     a. Call piece.getAvailableMoves(game, p).
     b. Append all returned moves to `allMoves`.
  4. Return `allMoves`.
Related Features: board, numMoves, configuration, currentPlayer (inherited from Game)
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Place, Move, Configuration
Input: player (Player) - the player whose legal moves are requested; must be non-null.
Output: List<Move> - the union of all legal moves of every piece owned by the player; empty if none.
Pre-condition: player is non-null and registered in the game; the board is in a consistent state.
Post-condition: The game state is unchanged; the returned list is freshly constructed and may be modified safely.

JesonMor::start
Summary: Drives the main game loop of JesonMor: alternates turns between the two registered players,
         fetches available moves, prompts each player for a move, executes it, updates the score,
         checks the win condition, and returns the eventual winner.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the configuration (size odd, numMovesProtection valid, two players present, initial pieces set);
     throw InvalidConfigurationError if invalid.
  2. Initialize game state (board from configuration.initialBoard, numMoves = 0, currentPlayer = players.get(0)).
  3. Call refreshOutput().
  4. Loop:
     a. availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer).
     b. If availableMoves is empty:
        - Let other = the opponent player; return getWinner(currentPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove)
          using the score-fallback rule (higher score wins, current player wins on tie).
     c. move = currentPlayer.nextMove(game, availableMoves).
     d. Record lastPlayer = currentPlayer, lastPiece = game.getPiece(move.source), lastMove = move.
     e. movePiece(move).
     f. updateScore(lastPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove).
     g. winner = getWinner(lastPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove).
     h. If winner is non-null, return winner.
     i. Switch currentPlayer to the other player and continue the loop.
Related Features: board, numMoves, configuration, currentPlayer (inherited from Game)
Related Classes: Game, Configuration, Player, ConsolePlayer, RandomPlayer, Move, Place, Piece, InvalidConfigurationError
Input: (none) - no parameters; operates on the game's internal configuration and players.
Output: Player - the winning player when the game terminates.
Pre-condition: configuration is valid (odd board size, two players, numMovesProtection >= 0,
               initial pieces placed within board); currentPlayer and opponent are set.
Post-condition: Returns the winner; the game has reached a terminal state (someone won or no-moves fallback).

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary: Adds the Manhattan distance between the move's source and destination to the given player's score.
Algorithm:
  1. If player, piece, or move is null, return without effect.
  2. distance = |destination.x - source.x| + |destination.y - source.y|.
  3. player.score += distance.
Related Features: score (inherited from Player)
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place
Input: player (Player) - the player whose score is to be updated.
       piece (Piece) - the piece that moved (reserved for future use, not strictly required by the formula).
       move (Move) - the move that was just executed; supplies source and destination coordinates.
Output: void - no return value.
Pre-condition: player, piece, and move are non-null; source and destination are valid board coordinates.
Post-condition: player.score is increased by the Manhattan distance of the executed move.

JesonMor::getWinner
Summary: Determines the winner of the game in compliance with the JesonMor win conditions and protection rules.
Algorithm:
  1. If game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection, return null (no winner during protection).
  2. Knight-leaves-central check:
     a. If lastPiece is a Knight and lastMove.source equals configuration.centralPlace
        and lastMove.destination does NOT equal configuration.centralPlace,
        return lastPlayer as the winner.
  3. Elimination check:
     a. Count the pieces on the board belonging to each player.
     b. If all opponent pieces have been captured (i.e. only lastPlayer still has pieces, or opponent count is 0),
        return lastPlayer as the winner.
  4. Score-fallback (called by the main loop when the current player has no available moves):
     a. If lastPlayer.score > opponentScore, return lastPlayer.
     b. If lastPlayer.score < opponentScore, return the opponent.
     c. If equal, return lastPlayer (current player wins ties).
  5. Otherwise return null (no winner yet).
Related Features: numMoves, configuration, currentPlayer (inherited from Game)
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Knight, Archer, Move, Place, Configuration
Input: lastPlayer (Player) - the player who just moved (or the current player with no moves).
       lastPiece (Piece) - the piece that was just moved.
       lastMove (Move) - the move that was just executed (source/destination consulted for central-square check).
Output: Player - the winning player, or null if no winner has been decided yet.
Pre-condition: lastPlayer is non-null; game state is consistent; the protection check has already been evaluated.
Post-condition: No state is modified; a single Player reference is returned.

# Requirement

```text
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
```

# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::movePiece
Summary: Executes a legal move on the 2D board array: transfers the piece at the source square to the
         destination square, increments the game move counter, and refreshes the console output.
         The move is assumed to have already passed validation by the caller.
Algorithm:
  1. If move is null, source or destination is null, or game.getPiece(source) is null, return without effect.
  2. Let piece = game.getPiece(source).
  3. Set game.getBoard()[destination.x][destination.y] = piece.
  4. Set game.getBoard()[source.x][source.y] = null.
  5. Increment game.numMoves by 1.
  6. Call game.refreshOutput() to update the console.
Related Features: board, numMoves, configuration, currentPlayer (inherited from Game)
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input: move (Move) - the move to execute; source must contain a piece, destination is the new position.
Output: void - no return value.
Pre-condition: move is non-null; source contains a piece; the move has already been validated as legal;
               source and destination are within board bounds.
Post-condition: The source square is null; the destination square contains the moved piece; game.numMoves
               has been incremented by 1; the console has been refreshed.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Aggregates the legal moves of every piece belonging to the given player by delegating to each
         piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position) and concatenating the results without further filtering.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize an empty result list `allMoves`.
  2. Determine the player's piece positions by scanning the board for pieces whose `player` equals
     the supplied player.
  3. For each such piece at place `p`:
     a. Call piece.getAvailableMoves(game, p).
     b. Append all returned moves to `allMoves`.
  4. Return `allMoves`.
Related Features: board, numMoves, configuration, currentPlayer (inherited from Game)
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Place, Move, Configuration
Input: player (Player) - the player whose legal moves are requested; must be non-null.
Output: List<Move> - the union of all legal moves of every piece owned by the player; empty if none.
Pre-condition: player is non-null and registered in the game; the board is in a consistent state.
Post-condition: The game state is unchanged; the returned list is freshly constructed and may be modified safely.

JesonMor::start
Summary: Drives the main game loop of JesonMor: alternates turns between the two registered players,
         fetches available moves, prompts each player for a move, executes it, updates the score,
         checks the win condition, and returns the eventual winner.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the configuration (size odd, numMovesProtection valid, two players present, initial pieces set);
     throw InvalidConfigurationError if invalid.
  2. Initialize game state (board from configuration.initialBoard, numMoves = 0, currentPlayer = players.get(0)).
  3. Call refreshOutput().
  4. Loop:
     a. availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer).
     b. If availableMoves is empty:
        - Let other = the opponent player; return getWinner(currentPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove)
          using the score-fallback rule (higher score wins, current player wins on tie).
     c. move = currentPlayer.nextMove(game, availableMoves).
     d. Record lastPlayer = currentPlayer, lastPiece = game.getPiece(move.source), lastMove = move.
     e. movePiece(move).
     f. updateScore(lastPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove).
     g. winner = getWinner(lastPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove).
     h. If winner is non-null, return winner.
     i. Switch currentPlayer to the other player and continue the loop.
Related Features: board, numMoves, configuration, currentPlayer (inherited from Game)
Related Classes: Game, Configuration, Player, ConsolePlayer, RandomPlayer, Move, Place, Piece, InvalidConfigurationError
Input: (none) - no parameters; operates on the game's internal configuration and players.
Output: Player - the winning player when the game terminates.
Pre-condition: configuration is valid (odd board size, two players, numMovesProtection >= 0,
               initial pieces placed within board); currentPlayer and opponent are set.
Post-condition: Returns the winner; the game has reached a terminal state (someone won or no-moves fallback).

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary: Adds the Manhattan distance between the move's source and destination to the given player's score.
Algorithm:
  1. If player, piece, or move is null, return without effect.
  2. distance = |destination.x - source.x| + |destination.y - source.y|.
  3. player.score += distance.
Related Features: score (inherited from Player)
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place
Input: player (Player) - the player whose score is to be updated.
       piece (Piece) - the piece that moved (reserved for future use, not strictly required by the formula).
       move (Move) - the move that was just executed; supplies source and destination coordinates.
Output: void - no return value.
Pre-condition: player, piece, and move are non-null; source and destination are valid board coordinates.
Post-condition: player.score is increased by the Manhattan distance of the executed move.

JesonMor::getWinner
Summary: Determines the winner of the game in compliance with the JesonMor win conditions and protection rules.
Algorithm:
  1. If game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection, return null (no winner during protection).
  2. Knight-leaves-central check:
     a. If lastPiece is a Knight and lastMove.source equals configuration.centralPlace
        and lastMove.destination does NOT equal configuration.centralPlace,
        return lastPlayer as the winner.
  3. Elimination check:
     a. Count the pieces on the board belonging to each player.
     b. If all opponent pieces have been captured (i.e. only lastPlayer still has pieces, or opponent count is 0),
        return lastPlayer as the winner.
  4. Score-fallback (called by the main loop when the current player has no available moves):
     a. If lastPlayer.score > opponentScore, return lastPlayer.
     b. If lastPlayer.score < opponentScore, return the opponent.
     c. If equal, return lastPlayer (current player wins ties).
  5. Otherwise return null (no winner yet).
Related Features: numMoves, configuration, currentPlayer (inherited from Game)
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Knight, Archer, Move, Place, Configuration
Input: lastPlayer (Player) - the player who just moved (or the current player with no moves).
       lastPiece (Piece) - the piece that was just moved.
       lastMove (Move) - the move that was just executed (source/destination consulted for central-square check).
Output: Player - the winning player, or null if no winner has been decided yet.
Pre-condition: lastPlayer is non-null; game state is consistent; the protection check has already been evaluated.
Post-condition: No state is modified; a single Player reference is returned.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
OccupiedRule::validate
Summary: Prevents capturing a friendly piece: the destination must not contain a piece belonging to the
         same player as the source piece.
Algorithm:
  1. If game, move, source, or destination is null, return false.
  2. sourcePiece = game.getPiece(source).
  3. destPiece = game.getPiece(destination).
  4. If destPiece is null, return true (empty square is always allowed at this stage).
  5. If destPiece.player equals sourcePiece.player, return false.
  6. Otherwise (opponent piece) return true.
Related Features: getDescription (inherited from Rule)
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, Player
Input: game (Game) - the live game state used to inspect both squares.
       move (Move) - the move to validate.
Output: boolean - true if destination is empty or occupied by an opponent piece; false if friendly.
Pre-condition: game and move are non-null; source and destination are within board bounds.
Post-condition: No state is modified.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
ArcherMoveRule::validate
Summary: Validates that a candidate move conforms to the Archer's orthogonal sliding and capture-jumping mechanics.
Algorithm:
  1. If move is null or source/destination is null, return false.
  2. Compute dx = destination.x - source.x, dy = destination.y - source.y.
  3. If the move is not strictly orthogonal (i.e., not (dx == 0 XOR dy == 0)) or dx == dy == 0, return false.
  4. Walk every intermediate square between source and destination (exclusive of both endpoints):
     a. Count how many squares contain any piece.
  5. Let destPiece = game.getPiece(destination).
  6. If destPiece is null (non-capturing move): require the intermediate count to be 0. Return true if so.
  7. If destPiece is non-null (capturing move): require the intermediate count to be exactly 1
     (the "screen" piece). Return true if so.
  8. Otherwise return false.
Related Features: getDescription (inherited from Rule)
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input: game (Game) - the live game state used to inspect the board between source and destination.
       move (Move) - the move to validate; its source and destination must be on the board.
Output: boolean - true if and only if the move is a legal Archer move.
Pre-condition: game is non-null, move is non-null, source and destination are within board bounds.
Post-condition: No state is modified.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
OutOfBoundaryRule::validate
Summary: Verifies that both the source and destination squares lie within the board's dimensions.
Algorithm:
  1. If game, move, source, or destination is null, return false.
  2. size = game.configuration.size.
  3. If source.x < 0 or source.x >= size or source.y < 0 or source.y >= size, return false.
  4. If destination.x < 0 or destination.x >= size or destination.y < 0 or destination.y >= size, return false.
  5. Otherwise return true.
Related Features: getDescription (inherited from Rule)
Related Classes: Game, Configuration, Move, Place
Input: game (Game) - the current game state providing the board size via configuration.
       move (Move) - the move to validate.
Output: boolean - true if both endpoints are inside the board, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: game and move are non-null; configuration.size > 0.
Post-condition: No state is modified.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
Piece::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Abstract template method. Subclasses (Knight, Archer) must override this method to return
         their own legal moves. The base implementation is undefined; the contract guarantees that
         every concrete piece returns only moves that have passed ALL applicable rules.
Algorithm:
  1. Default behavior: throw UnsupportedOperationException (this method is abstract).
  2. Subclass contract: generate piece-specific candidate destinations, validate each candidate against
     the global rule set and the piece's own rules, and return the surviving moves.
Related Features: player, getLabel
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Knight, Archer
Input: game (Game) - the current game state.
       source (Place) - the square occupied by the piece.
Output: List<Move> - the set of legal moves for the piece; empty list if none are available.
Pre-condition: game is non-null; source is non-null and within board bounds; game.getPiece(source) is this piece.
Post-condition: The game state is unchanged; the returned list contains only legal moves.

Piece::getLabel
Summary: Returns the single-character display label for the piece as required by the board rendering
         convention (Knight = 'K', Archer = 'A').
Algorithm:
  1. Default behavior: throw UnsupportedOperationException (this method is abstract).
  2. Knight.getLabel returns 'K'; Archer.getLabel returns 'A'.
Related Features: player
Related Classes: Knight, Archer
Input: (none) - takes no parameters.
Output: char - the character label that represents the piece on the rendered board.
Pre-condition: The concrete subclass implements this method.
Post-condition: No state is modified.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

```text
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
Archer::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Returns the list of legal moves available for an Archer piece located at the specified source square.
         It applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule,
         FirstNMovesProtectionRule) and the piece-specific ArcherMoveRule, then aggregates the surviving moves.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize an empty result list `moves`.
  2. If `source` is null or game.getPiece(source) is not this Archer, return empty list.
  3. Create the global rule list: VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule.
  4. Generate all candidate destination squares by sliding orthogonally (up, down, left, right) from `source`
     up to the board edge.
  5. For each candidate destination `dest`, build a Move(source, dest) and validate it against every rule
     in the global rule list and the ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add the Move to `moves`.
  6. Return `moves`.
Related Features: player (inherited from Piece), getLabel
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, ArcherMoveRule
Input: game (Game) - the current game state providing board access, size, numMoves, configuration and pieces.
       source (Place) - the square whose Archer is queried; must not be null and must contain an Archer.
Output: List<Move> - every orthogonal (non-jumping) move that passes all applicable rules; empty list if none legal.
Pre-condition: game is non-null, source is non-null and within board bounds, game.getPiece(source) returns this Archer.
Post-condition: Each returned Move has a non-null source and destination and is guaranteed to satisfy every
               applicable rule; the game state is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
```

```java
   * Summary: Drives the main game loop of JesonMor: alternates turns between the two registered players,

   *         - If scores are equal, return currentPlayer (current player wins ties).
```

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
   *          FirstNMovesProtectionRule) and the piece-specific ArcherMoveRule, then aggregates the surviving moves.

   *   1. Initialize an empty result list `moves`.
   *   2. If `source` is null or game.getPiece(source) is not this Archer, return empty list.
   *   3. Create the global rule list: VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule.
   *   4. Generate all candidate destination squares by enumerating every orthogonal square (up, down, left, right)

   *   5. For each candidate destination `dest`, build a Move(source, dest) and validate it against every rule
   *      in the global rule list and the ArcherMoveRule. The ArcherMoveRule accepts a candidate only when the
   *      path between source and destination contains 0 pieces (non-capture with a clear path) or exactly 1 piece
   *      of any color (capture with a "screen"/"mount" as in Chinese chess Cannon). If all rules pass, add the
   *      Move to `moves`.

   *        source (Place) - the square whose Archer is queried; must not be null and must contain an Archer.
   * Output: List<Move> - all legal orthogonal moves (non-capture moves with a clear path, and capture moves with
   *         exactly one "screen" piece of any color in between) that pass all applicable rules; empty list if none legal.

    }
```

    EList<Rule> rules = new BasicEList<Rule>();
    rules.add(Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule());

    rules.add(Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOccupiedRule());
    rules.add(Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule());
    rules.add(Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createArcherMoveRule());

    for (int[] d : directions)

      while (nx >= 0 && nx < size && ny >= 0 && ny < size)

            break;

        }

        if (valid)

        }

        nx += dx;
        ny += dy;
      }
    }

    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    
    if (source == null || destination == null)
    {
      return false;
    }
    
    int sourceX = source.getX();
    int sourceY = source.getY();
    int destX = destination.getX();
    int destY = destination.getY();
    
    int dx = destX - sourceX;
    int dy = destY - sourceY;
    
    int absDx = Math.abs(dx);
    int absDy = Math.abs(dy);
    
    int blockX;
    int blockY;
    
    if (absDx == 2 && absDy == 1)
    {
      blockX = (sourceX + destX) / 2;
      blockY = sourceY;
    }
    else if (absDx == 1 && absDy == 2)
    {
      blockX = sourceX;
      blockY = (sourceY + destY) / 2;
    }
    else
    {
      return false;
    }
    
    Piece blockingPiece = game.getPiece(blockX, blockY);
    
    if (blockingPiece != null)
    {
      return false;
    }
    
    return true;
  }

  public String getDescription()
  { ... /* omitted */ }

} // KnightBlockRule

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Validates that a candidate move conforms to the Archer's orthogonal sliding and capture-jumping mechanics.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If move is null or source/destination is null, return false.
   *   2. Compute dx = destination.x - source.x, dy = destination.y - source.y.
   *   3. If the move is not strictly orthogonal (i.e., not (dx == 0 XOR dy == 0)) or dx == dy == 0, return false.
   *   4. Walk every intermediate square between source and destination (exclusive of both endpoints):
   *      a. Count how many squares contain any piece.
   *   5. Let destPiece = game.getPiece(destination).
   *   6. If destPiece is null (non-capturing move): require the intermediate count to be 0. Return true if so.
   *   7. If destPiece is non-null (capturing move): require the intermediate count to be exactly 1
   *      (the "screen" piece, which may be of any color). Return true if so.
   *   8. Otherwise return false.
   * Related Features: None
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
   * Input: game (Game) - the live game state used to inspect the board between source and destination.
   *        move (Move) - the move to validate; its source and destination must be on the board.
   * Output: boolean - true if and only if the move is a legal Archer move.
   * Pre-condition: game is non-null, move is non-null, source and destination are within board bounds.
   * Post-condition: No state is modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    // Step 1: Null checks
    if (move == null || move.getSource() == null || move.getDestination() == null)
    {
      return false;
    }

    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();

    // Step 2: Compute dx, dy
    int dx = destination.getX() - source.getX();
    int dy = destination.getY() - source.getY();

    // Step 3: Strictly orthogonal check (XOR) and not zero movement
    if (!((dx == 0) ^ (dy == 0)))
    {
      return false;
    }

    if (dx == 0 && dy == 0)
    {
      return false;
    }

    // Step 4: Walk intermediate squares, counting pieces
    int intermediateCount = 0;
    int stepX = Integer.compare(dx, 0);
    int stepY = Integer.compare(dy, 0);

    int curX = source.getX() + stepX;
    int curY = source.getY() + stepY;

    while (curX != destination.getX() || curY != destination.getY())
    {
      if (game.getPiece(curX, curY) != null)
      {
        intermediateCount++;
      }
      curX += stepX;
      curY += stepY;
    }

    // Step 5: Get destination piece
    Piece destPiece = game.getPiece(destination);

    // Step 6 & 7: Validate based on capture status
    if (destPiece == null)
    {
      return intermediateCount == 0;
    }
    else
    {
      return intermediateCount == 1;
    }
  }

    // EMF 默认的 equals 往往是引用比较，保险起见采用坐标值比对
    Place central = this.getCentralPlace();
    if (central != null && place.getX() == central.getX() && place.getY() == central.getY()) {
        throw new InvalidConfigurationError("piece cannot be put at central place initially");
    }
    
    // 获取二维数组并赋值
    edu.pa20.Piece[][] board = this.getInitialBoard();
    if (board != null) {
        board[place.getX()][place.getY()] = piece;
    }
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='manual'"
   * @generated
   */
  public void addInitialPiece(final Piece piece, final int x, final int y)
  {
    // 使用 EMF Factory 实例化 Place
    Place tempPlace = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
    tempPlace.setX(x);
    tempPlace.setY(y);
    
    // 调用已经适配好的 addInitialPiece(Piece piece, Place place)
    this.addInitialPiece(piece, tempPlace);
  }
